text:
maria: Heads-up: new flaky failure in the edge sample apps when built with different bundlers. Looks like bundlers pick the wrong entry and TypeScript emit + cjs interop cause `require` to show up in worker bundles.

sam: repro I used:
- clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-edge-sdk-minimal
- npm ci && npm run build:vite && npx miniflare dist/worker.js
Result: RuntimeError: ReferenceError: require is not defined (stack points into chunk that imports crypto).

maria: Important nuance: our published @redwood-inference/sdk currently has `main` -> dist/index.cjs.js and `module` -> dist/index.esm.js but no "exports" map. Some bundlers rely on package.exports or conditional exports and others fall back to heuristics.

li: I saw a different failure with rollup + ssr: `The requested module '.../dist/index.cjs.js' does not provide an export named 'default'` — because rollup resolved the CJS file as an ES module import.

zack: Related type/tsconfig issue: our TS build emits `import x = require('y')` in some helper transforms when `esModuleInterop` is false; that forces rollup-plugin-commonjs to wrap things and sometimes produce `require()` calls in final ESM bundles.

maria: Quick local mitigation: change the sample's package resolution by pointing to the ESM file explicitly in vite/webpack alias: `@redwood-inference/sdk` -> `/node_modules/@redwood-inference/sdk/dist/esm/index.js`. Confirms entry selection is the cause. Not a long-term fix.

sam: Proposed SDK fixes (short):
1) publish dual layout: dist/esm/* (pure ESM), dist/cjs/* (CJS)
2) add conditional exports + subpath exports (import/require, ./package.json)
3) run a bundler smoke matrix in CI that builds sample apps with vite/webpack/rollup and runs them in miniflare/wrangler/puppeteer for browser edge checks

li: Also add a lint/compile check: ensure no `require(` tokens in ESM outputs (simple grep in release pipeline).

zack: For the SDK build: switch TS target to ES2020 module output for ESM dist and enable `preserveValueImports` and `esModuleInterop: true` for consistent emit; run rollup to bundle ESM with no commonjs plugin for that artifact. Keep a separate step to produce CJS with commonjs plugin.

ops-bot: CI job `sdk-edge-smoke` failed on 1745554300 -> see https://ci.redwood-inference/internal/edge-smoke/418. Error: "ReferenceError: require is not defined" in worker start.

maria: Can someone pick up a PR? Minimal checklist for the PR: add exports map, add dist/esm publish artifact, update release pipeline to run smoke builds, and add a short changelog entry. Add a tiny integration test that imports the SDK from the sample via the real package name (not file path) and runs a worker start in CI.

sam: I'll open the PR for exports + smoke CI. I'll also add a `grep -R "\brequire\(" dist/esm || exit 1` check in the release job.

li: I'll follow-up with a small TypeScript config cleanup and ensure rollup's commonjs plugin only runs for the CJS artifact.

maria: Thanks. Filing an oncall note for support with suggested temporary workarounds: 1) pin previous SDK that had explicit exports, 2) add vite alias to ESM entry, 3) try `esModuleInterop` toggles if building from source.

zack: One more edge case: some bundlers try to resolve `exports` import condition based on `browser` or `import` fields. Make sure we add `exports` AND keep `module` for older bundlers.

maria: Awesome. Adding @product to prioritize communication. :eyes:
